newsitem.title: USA: Glens Falls, N.Y., mulls $33 mln utility revs.
newsitem.headline: Glens Falls, N.Y., mulls $33 mln utility revs.

text.p: Voters in Glens Falls, N.Y., will decide whether the city should issue $33 million in bonds for its own electric utlility or remain with Niagara Mohawk Power Corp, the Albany Times Union said.
The proposal is backed by Ray Mahoney, chairman of the Glens Falls Industrial Development Agency, and the agency has played a key role with getting it on the November 5 ballot.

A study found the city's electricity rates would drop up to 40 to 50 percent rates even after it spent $33 million to take over Nagara Mohawk Power's local power operations and paid other start-up costs, the paper said in its Tuesday edition.
Municipal law allows Glens Falls, which now pays $23 million for electricty to Niagara Mohawk every year, to buy the company's properties under the right of emminent domain.

The paper added that the company, and citizens who oppose the proposal, have formed a committee to fight it. It quoted a spokesman for Niagara Mohawk as saying that the deregulation of the power market will accomplish the proposal's goal, which is getting lower electricity rates.
